statements.status_notes: CVE-2024-53427 (GHSA-x6c3-qv5r-7q22, https://github.com/jqlang/jq/security/advisories/GHSA-x6c3-qv5r-7q22): decNumberCopy() in jq 1.7 and 1.7.1 does not treat NaN as numeric, so input such as '1 NaN123' followed by many digits, processed with --slurp and a filter like .-., causes a stack buffer overflow (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/issues/3196). Upstream fixed it in jq 1.8.0 with https://github.com/jqlang/jq/commit/b86ff49f46a4a37e5a8e75a140cb5fd6e1331384 and https://github.com/jqlang/jq/commit/a09a4dfd55e6c24d04b35062ccfe4509748b1dd3. Checked every jq build in the DHI Debian 13 repository for amd64 and arm64, using the changelog each package ships and its libjq: rebuilds of Debian 1.7.1-6+deb13u1 and 1.7.1-6+deb13u2, a 1.8.1-5 build (arm64 only) whose changelog is an unreleased Debian 1.8.1-5 snapshot from January 2026 with no 2026 security fixes, and a rebuild of Debian 1.8.2-1, which is upstream jq 1.8.2. Debian's 1.7.1-5 patch had no effect: the 1.7.1-6+deb13u3 changelog fixes it 'for real' because 'NaN123' still parsed, and Debian records trixie as fixed only in 1.7.1-6+deb13u3 (DSA-6416-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2024-53427), which has no DHI rebuild. Given the input NaN123, the arm64 1.7.1 rebuilds print null, while the 1.8.1-5 build and the rebuild of 1.8.2-1 reject it as an invalid literal. The boundary is the rebuild of 1.8.2-1, the first build in the current version scheme with the fix; the 1.8.1-5 build also contains the fix but sorts below it and reads as affected.
